title: dedicated-autoscaler-smoothing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler with smoothing for burst token buckets and updates utilization reporting to avoid transient double-counting during bursts. Includes metric and dashboard updates.
description:
Context and motivation:
Our Dedicated fleet saw repeated oscillations when customers with bursty workloads (short, high-throughput bursts) hit tokenbucket limits. The current autoscaler reacts to instantaneous utilization spikes which triggers scaling decisions and leads to overshoot and churn. Additionally, utilization reporting in the console was double-counting KV-cache warmup and burst allocation, inflating short-term utilization numbers and making SLO dashboards noisy.

What this PR does:
- Implements a smoothing layer in the Dedicated autoscaler token-bucket plumbing: an exponential moving average (EMA) over a configurable time window (default 30s) for both observed token consumption and queue depth.
- Adds a burst-credit accounting correction so that short-lived burst allocations are attributed to a transient bucket usage metric rather than steady-state utilization, preventing them from affecting scale-to-target computations.
- Updates utilization reporting pipeline to separate "steady_utilization" and "burst_allocation" metrics, and prevents the dashboard aggregate from double-counting KV cache warmups during burst handoff.
- Adds feature flag (feature.autoscaler.smoothing = true) and rollout plan to enable smoothing gradually per-customer.
- Adds unit and integration tests that simulate bursty traffic patterns and assert stable scaling decisions and correct metric emission.

Design notes and reasoning:
- Smoothing window chosen as EMA with alpha computed from window size to favor fast response to real sustained load while damping single-request spikes. We evaluated 10s/30s/60s windows against our perf canary traces; 30s showed best tradeoff for Dedicated fleets with 1s token refill granularity.
- We keep burst credits orthogonal to steady-state throughput so that short bursts do not immediately move the target desired_replicas. The autoscaler still guarantees throughput by allowing controlled short-term oversubscription via burst credits.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior invariant (smoothing disabled) until flag is turned on for customers; metric names are additive.

Files & changes summary (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/controller.go: main EMA smoothing loop + configuration parsing and feature-flag gating.
- pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go: new burst credit accounting and corrected consumption recording.
- pkg/metrics/reporting.go: emits steady_utilization and burst_allocation metrics; migration layer for old metric names.
- internal/test/fixtures/bursty_workload_test.go: end-to-end tests covering scale-up/scale-down decisions.
- charts/redwood-helm-charts/templates/autoscaler.yaml: new feature flag and defaults.
- docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md: design doc and rollout instructions.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag off by default.
- Canary rollout to internal Dedicated fleet for 24h with enhanced logging and a rollback script.
- Gradual ramp to 10% of Dedicated customers for 72h and monitor per-tenant scaling churn and per-route 95th latency.
- Metrics to watch: autoscaler.desired_replicas_delta, autoscaler.scale_events_per_min, metric steady_utilization, burst_allocation, and console dashboard noise score.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests for EMA math and burst-credit edge cases.
- Integration test harness that replays production burst traces (anonymized) and asserts no more than 1 unnecessary replica add/remove per 10m under bursty conditions.
- CI: all tests passed after a single flaky rerun on the integration job.

Related work and follow-ups:
- Follow-up PR will add per-model smoothing windows based on model size and latency SLOs (ENG-4876).
- Observability: add a Grafana alert to detect unexpected steady_utilization jumps (ENG-4821).

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation code + unit tests
- [x] Integration test harness
- [x] Docs updated (docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md)
- [x] Helm chart flag added
- [x] Rollout plan and rollback script included

Impacts & notes:
- No API or customer-visible config changes by default. Customers opting into smoothing may see fewer scale oscillations and slightly longer cold-start latencies during very short bursts due to delayed scale decisions (intended tradeoff).

Merge notes:
- Squash-merged after approvals.
